::: {.why}
The machinery from this week is only worth having if signals are cheap to add, and building three in one hour is the test of whether it is.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Implement three signals through the interface with no strategy-specific plumbing.
- Have each one produce a result object through the engine with no code changes to the engine.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Build three signals in qlib/signals/: 12-month price momentum skipping the most recent month, 1-month reversal, and 60-day realised volatility with the sign you decide and defend. Each is a subclass of the base interface, each declares its units, each states its economic rationale in the docstring.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Run all three through the engine with the standard transform, neutralisation and weight map, and produce three result objects. If any of them required touching the engine, the interface is wrong and fixing it now is cheaper than in week 29.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
Three signals are in the book, each implemented through the same interface and run through the same pipeline. Adding the fourth is now a file rather than a project, which is the property the alpha book needs.
:::

## Resources

- [Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) — Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers](https://www.bauer.uh.edu/rsusmel/phd/jegadeesh-titman93.pdf) [paper]{.res-kind}

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
Three signals in qlib/signals/ with declared units and stated rationales, each producing a result object with no engine changes.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Why does momentum skip the most recent month, and what would happen to the signal if it did not?
:::
